subject: France
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about France's border with Brazil. Claims are cited to pinned Wikipedia revisions (trusted_secondary). Map geometry comes from Natural Earth (which draws French Guiana as part of France) and is not evidence for any claim.

claims.text: At 730 kilometres, the Brazil–France border is the longest border France shares with another country, despite not being in metropolitan France. The second longest is with Spain, at 623 kilometres.
French Guiana is an overseas department and region of France on the northern coast of South America, bordered by Suriname to the west and Brazil to the east and south.
The border separates the Brazilian state of Amapá from French Guiana and runs through the Amazon rainforest; the Oyapock River defines part of it.
The Oyapock River Bridge, between Saint-Georges (French Guiana) and Oiapoque (Brazil), is the only bridge crossing the border.
The border's basis dates to the Treaty of Utrecht of 1713; the dispute over it was resolved in Brazil's favour in 1900 by international arbitration in Switzerland.

oyapock-bridge.note: The bridge between Saint-Georges and Oiapoque.
